result:
I found 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them. I didn't touch the other 139.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | Capped the price at 30,000 before applying the discount; the common rule says the discount is what gets capped | Compute `base*5//100`, then cap at 30,000 |
| 15 | Marked whole, but only discounted units above the threshold (marginal) | `base * 10 // 100` |
| 27 | Threshold was `>= 101`, docstring says 100+ | `qty >= 100` |
| 40 | Cap only applied once the discount went over 60,000 | Always cap at 30,000 |
| 46 | Used 4%, docstring says 3% | 3% |
| 47 | Used `round()`, which rounds instead of flooring | `// 100` (floor) |
| 55 | Cap only applied once the discount went over 200,000 | Always cap at 100,000 |
| 59 | Used 3%, docstring says 2% | 2% |
| 106 | Threshold was `qty > 5`, docstring says 5+ | `qty >= 5` |
| 107 | Threshold was `qty > 50`, docstring says 50+ | `qty >= 50` |
| 124 | Marked whole, but computed the discount as marginal | `base * 7 // 100` |

**How I checked:**
- **Behaviour test:** I read each docstring into a reference formula and compared it with the real function. The test grid was quantities 0–399 plus a few large values, against 16 unit prices. It also confirmed negative input raises `ValueError` and every result is an `int`. Before the fixes, exactly these 11 rules mismatched; after, there are 0.
- **Code check:** I compared every function body against a standard template. Rules 18, 56, 58, 62, 66, 81, 104, 117, 121, 136 and 146 are written differently (e.g. `not qty < 30`, `5 <= qty`, `(qty * unit)`), but they compute the same result, so I left them alone. Rule 136 (marginal) uses `qty > 5`, but the discount at exactly 5 units is 0 either way.

STATUS: DONE
